etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English fume, from Old French fum (“smoke, steam, vapour”), from Latin fūmus (“vapour, smoke”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰuh₂mós (“smoke”), from *dʰewh₂- (“to smoke, raise dust”). Doublet of thymus and thymos. More at dun, dusk, dust.

definitions.definition: A gas or vapour/vapor that is strong-smelling or dangerous to inhale.
A material that has been vaporized from the solid or liquid state to the gas state and re-coalesced to the solid state.
Rage or excitement which deprives the mind of self-control.
